section: Citizenship - Articles 5-11; Citizenship Act 1955, acquisition and loss, OCI, CAA 2019
subsections: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods

accepted.s: A child born in India between 26 January 1950 and 30 June 1987 acquired citizenship by birth irrespective of the nationality of the parents, subject to the statutory exceptions. Which one of the following is one such exception?
o: A child whose one parent is an Indian citizen
A child born to two Indian citizens
A child whose birth is registered in India
accepted.x: Children of foreign diplomats and enemy aliens cannot acquire Indian citizenship by birth. The nationality of the parents was otherwise immaterial during this period.
accepted.tq: Use the exception trap in an otherwise broad birth-citizenship rule.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to citizenship by birth, consider the following statements:
1. A person born in India from 1 July 1987 to 2 December 2004 could acquire citizenship if at least one parent was an Indian citizen at the time of birth.
2. For a person born in India on or after 3 December 2004, both parents must necessarily be Indian citizens.
3. From 3 December 2004, one Indian-citizen parent is sufficient if the other parent is not an illegal migrant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because, from 3 December 2004, one parent may be an Indian citizen if the other is not an illegal migrant.
accepted.tq: Track the change in the birth rule across the three date ranges.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents citizenship by descent under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
o: Born outside India, with either parent being an Indian citizen at the time of birth, and birth registered at an Indian consulate
Born in India and one parent an Indian citizen
Born outside India and resident in India for five years
Born in a territory incorporated into India and notified by the Central Government
accepted.x: Citizenship by descent applies to a person born outside India when either parent was an Indian citizen at the time of birth, subject to registration of the birth at an Indian consulate.
accepted.tq: Distinguish descent from birth, registration and incorporation by location of birth.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Mode)
a. Birth
b. Descent
c. Naturalisation
d. Incorporation of territory

List-II (Condition)
i. Government specifies persons who become citizens when a territory joins India
ii. Birth outside India with an Indian-citizen parent and consular registration
iii. Ordinary residence and oath of allegiance
iv. Birth in India subject to the applicable parental conditions

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Birth relates to birth in India, descent to birth abroad with consular registration, naturalisation to residence and oath, and incorporation to a territory joining India.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched modes.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For ordinary naturalisation under the Citizenship Act, 1955, the residence requirement is best expressed as:
o: Five years of residence immediately preceding the application
Six months of residence followed by an oath of allegiance
Seven years of residence immediately preceding the application
Twelve years, comprising eleven years during the preceding fourteen years and the immediately preceding twelve months
accepted.x: Ordinary naturalisation requires twelve years in the statutory formulation: eleven years during the preceding fourteen years and the last twelve months immediately before the application, along with other conditions including the oath of allegiance.
accepted.tq: Split the aggregate residence period into its statutory components.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following conditions may be waived in the case of naturalisation for a person who has rendered distinguished service?
o: The oath of allegiance in every case
The requirement that the person must be a foreign national
The residence condition for distinguished service to science, art, literature or world peace
The power of the Central Government to grant citizenship
accepted.x: The residence conditions for naturalisation may be waived for persons who have rendered distinguished service in fields such as science, art, literature or the cause of world peace. The oath of allegiance remains a stated condition.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific condition that can be relaxed rather than treating all conditions as waivable.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A person of Indian origin seeks citizenship through registration. Which residence period is associated with the current rule mentioned for such registration?
accepted.x: The current residence period mentioned for registration of persons of Indian origin is seven years. The older reference to six months is not the current rule.
accepted.tq: Use the current-versus-older-rule distinction in a numerical question.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following persons is specifically associated with acquisition of citizenship by registration?
o: A spouse of an Indian citizen after fulfilling the prescribed residence condition
A foreign diplomat born in India
Every person who enters India without registration
An enemy alien born in India
accepted.x: Persons of Indian origin, spouses of Indian citizens and minor children of citizens are among the categories associated with citizenship by registration after the prescribed conditions are fulfilled.
accepted.tq: Match the applicant category with the correct statutory mode.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Marriage to an Indian citizen under the Citizenship Act, 1955 is:
o: A ground that automatically confers citizenship without any condition
A mode available only through incorporation of territory
A category dealt with through registration rather than a separate mode
A separate sixth mode of acquiring citizenship
accepted.x: Marriage is not an independent mode of acquisition. A spouse may qualify under the registration provisions after satisfying the prescribed conditions.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a separate mode and a category within registration.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: When a foreign territory becomes part of India, who specifies the persons who will become Indian citizens?
accepted.x: Under incorporation of territory, the Government of India specifies the persons who become citizens when the territory joins India.
accepted.tq: Ask who performs the statutory designation function.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding loss of Indian citizenship:
1. Renunciation takes place through a declaration by the citizen.
2. Termination follows automatically when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country.
3. Deprivation can be ordered by the Central Government in specified cases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The three modes of loss are renunciation, automatic termination on voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship, and deprivation by the Central Government in specified cases.
accepted.tq: Separate voluntary declaration, automatic consequence and governmental action.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a ground associated with deprivation of citizenship?
o: Marriage to a foreign national by itself
accepted.x: Deprivation may be connected with fraud, disloyalty or aiding an enemy, among specified grounds. Marriage to a foreign national by itself is not such a ground.
accepted.tq: Find the option that is not a statutory ground among closely related citizenship events.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Deprivation of citizenship by the Central Government may apply to citizens who acquired citizenship by:
1. Naturalisation
2. Registration
3. Article 5(c) of the Constitution
4. Birth in India in every case
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Deprivation may apply to citizens by naturalisation, registration and Article 5(c). It does not apply to citizens by birth in every case as stated in item 4.
accepted.tq: Check the scope of governmental power instead of assuming it applies to every citizen.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1986 is associated with which change?
o: Reduction of the naturalisation residence period to five years
Tightening of the citizenship-by-birth rule from 1 July 1987
Merger of PIO and OCI cards
accepted.x: The 1986 amendment tightened the birth rule, with the one-parent Indian-citizen requirement applying from 1 July 1987.
accepted.tq: Link the amendment year with its specific statutory change.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The PIO card was merged with the OCI card in 2015. The 2003 amendment related to the birth rule and OCI registration, while the CAA route belongs to 2019.
accepted.tq: Use amendment-year association and reject swapped-year traps.

accepted.s:
The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 is associated with which of the following?
1. The birth rule applicable from 3 December 2004
2. Introduction of OCI registration
3. Merger of PIO and OCI cards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 2003 amendment is associated with the birth rule effective from 3 December 2004 and the introduction of OCI registration. The PIO-OCI merger occurred in 2015.
accepted.tq: Use a statement combination to distinguish adjacent amendment years.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. PIO card merged with OCI
B. Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1986
C. Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003
D. Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1986 amendment, 2003 amendment, PIO-OCI merger in 2015, and CAA in 2019.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle developments.

accepted.s: In which of the following years was the Citizenship Act, 1955 NOT amended, according to the stated legislative chronology?
accepted.x: The stated chronology identifies 1986, 2003 and 2019 amendments, while 2008 is specified as a year in which the Act was not amended.
accepted.tq: Select the year that breaks the amendment sequence rather than the years linked to known changes.

accepted.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 reduced the naturalisation residence requirement for specified migrants to:
accepted.x: For the specified categories covered by the CAA, 2019, the naturalisation residence requirement was reduced to five years.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the CAA-specific reduction from the ordinary naturalisation period.

accepted.s:
Under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, the specified religious communities include:
1. Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist and Jain
2. Parsi and Christian
3. Muslim
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The specified communities are Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian. Muslims are not included in this CAA route.
accepted.tq: Test the exact enumerated list and identify the excluded community.

accepted.s: Which combination correctly describes the persons covered by the citizenship route introduced by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
o: Only Indian citizens by descent who reside in Pakistan
All migrants from every neighbouring country who entered India after 31 December 2014
Specified religious communities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered India on or before 31 December 2014
All foreign nationals who have completed five months in India
accepted.x: The CAA route covers Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered India on or before 31 December 2014.
accepted.tq: Combine community, country and cut-off-date conditions without dropping any element.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which areas are excluded from the operation of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 route?
o: All Union Territories and all border districts
All areas administered by District Collectors
Sixth Schedule tribal areas and Inner Line Permit areas
Only metropolitan cities and cantonment areas
accepted.x: The CAA route excludes areas covered by the Sixth Schedule and areas under the Inner Line Permit regime.
accepted.tq: Test the geographical exception rather than the general coverage of the Act.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the dates associated with the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 and its Rules?
o: Act on 11 March 2024; Rules effective on 12 December 2019
Act on 12 December 2019; Rules effective on 11 March 2024
Act on 31 December 2014; Rules effective on 12 December 2019
Act on 19 August 2026; Rules effective on 20 May 2026
accepted.x: The Act was enacted on 12 December 2019, while the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules became effective on 11 March 2024.
accepted.tq: Separate the enactment date from the date on which the Rules became effective.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026, which of the following is provided for?
o: Automatic citizenship for every OCI cardholder
Replacement of registration by incorporation of territory
accepted.x: The 2026 Rules provide for e-OCI cards. They do not abolish OCI cards or automatically confer citizenship on every OCI cardholder.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise administrative change while rejecting overbroad automatic-citizenship claims.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A CAA applicant holding a passport of Pakistan, Afghanistan or Bangladesh is required under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026 to:
o: Retain the passport permanently after approval
Exchange the passport for an OCI card within seven years
File an affidavit concerning the passport and surrender it within 15 days of approval
Surrender the passport before entering India and file no affidavit
accepted.x: The applicant must file an affidavit concerning the relevant passport and surrender the passport within 15 days after approval.
accepted.tq: Apply the procedural sequence and the exact fifteen-day time limit.
accepted.sec: Modes of acquiring citizenship under the Citizenship Act 1955 - number, conditions, residence periods  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the MHA order of 19 August 2026, CAA applications in the specified eight States and Union Territories are processed by:
o: Only the Union Public Service Commission
accepted.x: The 19 August 2026 MHA order transferred processing in the specified eight States and Union Territories to District Collectors instead of Empowered Committees.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-substitution trap: identify who performs the administrative function.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional litigation concerning the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 as stated?
o: 25 petitions concerning Article 21 were finally decided by a Bench under the Election Commission
The issue concerned only Article 32 and had no pending hearing
250-plus petitions were dismissed before the Rules came into force
250-plus petitions concerning Article 14 were pending before a Bench under CJI Surya Kant, with final hearing from 5 May 2026
accepted.x: More than 250 petitions involving Article 14 were pending before a Bench under CJI Surya Kant, with the final hearing scheduled from 5 May 2026 as stated.
accepted.tq: Combine the litigation number, constitutional provision, judicial bench and hearing date precisely.
